sections.h2: Who runs property tax in Bernalillo County
sections.html:
The work is divided between two elected offices that share Alvarado Square, 415 Silver Ave SW in Albuquerque, the county seat. One decides what your property is worth and builds the roll, and the other sends bills and takes money. The Assessor's number is (505) 222-3700 and the Treasurer's is (505) 468-7031.

Bernalillo County is New Mexico's most populous, with more than 676,000 residents, about 106,000 of them outside city limits in Albuquerque, Los Ranchos and Tijeras. Parcels run from city lots to unincorporated land, and the rate you pay hinges on the districts around your address.

The Assessor's job covers real property, business personal property, livestock and manufactured homes. It notifies owners of value and hands the finished roll to the Treasurer.

Value is fixed on January 1, notices go out by April 1, rates are set in September, the roll reaches the Treasurer by October 1, and bills are in the mail by early November.

EventTimingOffice
Property valued as of its conditionJanuary 1Assessor
Exemption and Head of Family applicationsEnd of February, or a month after the Notice of ValueAssessor
Notices of Value mailedBy April 1Assessor
Valuation certified to the stateJune 15Assessor
Delinquent notices mailedAbout June 10Treasurer
Rates setSeptemberState Dept. of Finance and Administration
Tax roll deliveredOctober 1Assessor to Treasurer
Bills mailed, first half dueNovember 1 and November 10Treasurer
Second half dueApril 10Treasurer

If November 1 lands on a weekend, bills go out the next business day. Anyone who is not on the 10-month payment agreement pays in one lump or in two installments.

Take one-third of assessed value to get taxable value. Subtract exemptions from it, and only then apply the mill rate. What remains is net taxable value, after items like Head of Family and the veteran exemption.

The state sets mill rates, and they differ by taxing district. The Treasurer posts rate charts for 2016 to 2025, and the Assessor's property search shows the figures for one address. In the latest cycle many rates fell, but rising valuations, a new taxing district and added tax initiatives still pushed bills up across the county.

Statewide, residential taxable value may grow at most 3% a year. That ceiling covers assessment growth, and the mill rate is a separate matter.

The Assessor handles Head of Family, veteran and disabled veteran exemptions, plus a value freeze. You do not file a protest form for any of them.

  • Head of Family takes $2,000 off taxable value for one property per household in the state.
  • The veteran exemption takes up to $10,000 off taxable value with a certificate from the state's veteran service commission. Once granted, it stays on the record.
  • A disabled veteran can exempt a share of the primary residence that matches the VA disability rating.
  • The value freeze serves owners aged 65 and over whose modified gross income is $42,900 or under, and disabled owners at $41,900 or under. It halts the 3% assessment increase but leaves the tax rate alone.

The deadline is a month after the Notice of Value goes out. The Assessor's tax savings page has the forms. A value freeze never forces you to sell at the frozen value.

Your protest goes to the Assessor, either through the online appeal portal or in person at 415 Silver Ave SW, and it must arrive within 30 days of the Notice of Value mailing. You then sit down informally with a field appraiser. If you and the appraiser still disagree, the Protest Valuation Review Board hears the matter. An amended Notice of Value restarts the 30 days from its own mailing date.

Business personal property, manufactured home and livestock protests run on a separate spring window, so check the Assessor's protest page each year.

If the window has closed, the fallback is paying in full and filing a refund claim at the Second Judicial District Court, 400 Lomas Blvd NW. The Treasurer puts the cutoff 60 days after the first installment due date. Payment comes first. The Assessor lists a $132 court filing fee. Call the court self-help center at 505-841-6702 to confirm the cutoff before you rely on it.

With a protest still open in December, pay the first half on the original bill, as the Treasurer advises. If you win, a new bill and a refund follow. If you lose, you have avoided late fees.

A late payment draws interest of 1% a month and, on top, a penalty of 1% a month that stops at 5% and never drops below $5. The clock starts December 10 for the first half and May 10 for the second.

You can pay in person on the first floor of 415 Silver Ave SW, online through the county's payment vendor, or by mail to PO Box 27800, Albuquerque, NM 87125-7800. The Treasurer warns against bank bill-pay services because of mailing delays, misrouting and no confirmation. Owners are liable even if a bill never arrives. About 10,600 bills came back undelivered in the 2025 cycle, mostly for outdated addresses, so keep your mailing address current.

Delinquent notices go out around June 10.

The January 1 owner owes that year's tax. A manufactured home additionally requires a tax release before it can be sold, moved or traded. The title company looks up what is due and settles it from your proceeds.

A manufactured home owner gets the tax release from the Treasurer, showing current and prior years paid, and starts the process at the Assessor with proof of ownership. Land and a manufactured home on it get separate notices and bills unless the home has been converted to real property. Public improvement district charges transfer to the buyer, and a seller can prepay the balance.

Our Bernalillo County Clerk guide explains the residential transfer affidavit that the Assessor expects after closing. Some owners carrying back taxes, an inherited house or a tenant pick an as-is cash sale so they can skip repairs and showings. The tax still gets paid from the proceeds.

Ahead of listing, get the balance from the Treasurer, an exemption check from the Assessor, and a heads-up to the title company about any open protest.

sections.h2: Preparing to sell in Bernalillo County
sections.html:
A little groundwork saves days at closing. Begin by collecting the Treasurer's figures for both halves of this year, and ask the Assessor which exemptions are attached to the parcel. Tell your title company whether a protest is open, because a pending case can change the figure the buyer's side expects.

Keep your mailing address current. About 10,600 bills came back undelivered in the 2025 cycle, so an old address is common and avoidable. If your home was inherited or has a tenant, collect any estate or lease papers before you list, because the title company is going to request them.

Selling as-is for cash is an option for owners who would rather avoid repairs and showings. What the county is owed stays the same, so the payoff steps do not change.

faqs.q: When are Bernalillo County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Plan on November 10 for the first half and April 10 for the second. Late fees start December 10 and May 10.

faqs.q: Who sets property values in Bernalillo County?
faqs.a: The elected County Assessor sets values and mails Notices of Value by April 1. The elected Treasurer sends bills and collects. Each September the state fixes the mill rates.

faqs.q: How do I protest my Bernalillo County valuation?
faqs.a: Submit a protest form to the Assessor online or at 415 Silver Ave SW, no more than 30 days after the Notice of Value is mailed. An informal meeting comes first, then a Protest Valuation Review Board hearing if needed.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Bernalillo County house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company ordinarily pays the balance, penalty and interest included, from your closing proceeds. Confirm the figure with the Treasurer at (505) 468-7031.

faqs.q: Does Bernalillo County send a bill if a mortgage company pays my taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Every owner gets a bill even if a lender pays it. The bill names the mortgage company that requested the amount, and you are still the one who has to confirm it was paid.
